classifications.rationale: Generated identifiers do not become Thompson public exports or native test IDs.
The existing Thompson public component remains the owner.
The fixture and native implementation are both atomic controls.
Native visible and assistive labels share the consumer-owned string.
The semantic root stays a button while React Native owns the primitive.
React Native has no DOM span; Thompson owns native text rendering.
The semantic background role maps to Thompson's existing theme token.
Thompson preserves contrast with a theme-specific native foreground.
The existing portable button radius is authoritative.
The public Thompson variant already expresses the selected intent.
No native adaptation is required for the default state.
React Native derives press state from the input system instead of accepting generated state.
Thompson blocks input and publishes the native accessibility state.
Thompson owns the native activity indicator and blocks duplicate activation.
iOS and Android focus services own native focus; no DOM focus ring or generated focus command is installed.

classifications.target: none for the touch-first iOS/Android baseline
classifications.rationale: Hover is not treated as a portable mobile state and cannot silently become press or focus.
The native input event invokes a Thompson-owned callback.
The application owns routing and side effects; the design contract only names intent.
The selected fixture does not require an image, icon, or font payload.
